final_answer: The sky appears blue during the day due to Rayleigh scattering, where shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) scatter more efficiently than longer ones (red/orange). This occurs because Rayleigh scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength (I ∝ 1/λ⁴). Human eyes are more sensitive to blue light, and the scattered blue light fills the sky. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering most of the blue light out of the line of sight. The remaining light, dominated by longer wavelengths (red/orange), reaches the observer, creating the reddish hue.
